doc.title: Dave Rivello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012

chapter: Listening, jazz history and the future
title: Time-machine wishes: Thad Jones-Mel Lewis, Gil Evans, Rite of Spring
summary: He would visit the first Thad Jones-Mel Lewis night in 1966, Gil Evans at Sweet Basil, and Stravinsky's premiere.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: If you could go back in a time machine, any spots in the history of jazz that you wish you could descend into?

I guess with my world I would wish that I could have been there in 1966 I think it was, the Village Vanguard, the first night of the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band. I would wish that at some point I could have, which I never had the chance to do, just been in the room, even if it was the electric band of Gil Evans at Sweet Basil, but just to have experienced what it felt like to be in the room, the same room that Gil Evans was in. And non-jazz, but I wish I could have seen the premier of “The Rite of Spring.” Because for me that’s still the most incredible piece of music maybe ever written, all music included. “The Rite of Spring” for me, that’s the thing.

Yeah, that it came out of Stravinsky, but there’s not really a clear connection that I’ve found of like oh well he took some of this and he moved it that much further. It was like, again, a whole new world. And he wrote it in some little tiny room with no heat in Switzerland or something.
Maybe that’s why it sounds like it does.
Could be. He was just wanting to be warm. That’s why he was pounding on the piano — those chords that are in the strings.
